hash_of: sha256 of the file with line endings normalised to LF. That is what was deployed: scripts/deploy.py reads the file with universal newlines, so the bytes on chain are LF whatever a Windows checkout with autocrlf put on disk.
why: Every published number is tied to this pair of addresses. verify.py lints the deployed bytes against these files, RESULTS.md and HELD-OUT.md name the instance they were measured on, and the refusal and rail transactions in the README were recorded against these contracts. A redeploy invalidates all of it and costs 63 consensus transactions to restore.
if_a_change_is_genuinely_required: python eval/run.py --set v2 --runs 3 --out eval/results-v2.json && python eval/report.py --results eval/results-v2.json --out eval/RESULTS-V2.md
update contracts/FROZEN.json, README addresses and every published number, in the same commit
